title: PG-19.3 Shared pure replay of a project's event log for the project store and the read-only reader (memev)
request: Programme contract PG-19.3 in memev: one shared, pure replay of a project's event log, so that the project store and the read-only reader of PG-19.2 cannot drift. Proposed and unsigned; the signer signs it after the red-team gate. It is version 3 of PG-19 and does not supersede PG-19.2: it changes the body of the reader that PG-19.2 specified and keeps every criterion of PG-19.2. Why: the project store replays its log in ProjectStore#_replay and #_applyRecord (src/engine/project-store.mjs), and Vault#tasksReader in src/engine/vault.mjs, added by pull request #365 (PG-19.2, signed), replays the same log by a copy of those rules, because the reader must not open the store (opening it rewrites every snapshot, cuts a torn last line and takes no lock, which beside a live daemon changes files and can cut a line the daemon is still writing). The two are held together only by tests: the review of #365 found three places where the reader's replay differed from the store's, and its description names this contract as the follow-up. This contract makes the replay one pure function in a new module with no import, src/engine/project-replay.mjs, and moves both callers onto it. ORDER: pull request #365 lands first, with its duplicate replay and its stronger agreement test (decided at its review). This contract is signed and built after #365 has merged, and it is the side that adapts: the store and the reader move onto the shared function, #365 changes nothing. This spec records no base: the signer's HEAD after #365 has merged is the base the signature records, and the criteria that name Vault#tasksReader, src/cli/work-store.mjs, test/cli-work.test.mjs and test/cli-work-e2e.test.mjs are written for that HEAD, not for a commit before #365, where they are absent. The signed criteria of PG-19.2 are not superseded here and are judged at the merge commit of #365 (they check, among other things, that one method is added and that only vault.mjs changes, which stays true there and would not at a later HEAD); the register row for that is for the red-team to add. At the head of #365 the store's byte cut is wrong, so WP19-05 AC03 is red there by the real defect. Code is named by symbol, never by line, because the line numbers of #365 move when it is pushed again. What the shared function keeps: it reads and reports only. The truncation of a torn last line, the rewrite of snapshots, the lock and the migration stay in the store; the function has a truncate option, on for the store and off for the reader, that decides only whether it reports the cut for the caller to make. An unterminated last line is never applied by either caller, as the store does today. Both callers refuse a schema version above the supported one with future_schema; a project at an older version needs_migration for the reader and is migrated by the store; a project with a meta.json and no log gives an empty reader; an unknown project gives null. The reader's surface is unchanged and stays silent: a frozen object with one member, snapshot(kind), also frozen, returning structuredClone copies, needing a read credential, with no way to reach the store, and no notice on it. The shared function returns the notices; where they show is left to a later spec. The reader is a point-in-time view: it replays once when Vault#tasksReader() is called, snapshot(kind) returns structuredClone copies of that state, it is not live, and the work command is one-shot (WP19-05 AC09). Five deviations from the store as it is today are made on purpose and stated, each one its own named criterion with its own assertion-based red test, so that a reviewer can sign or strike each separately: A, the byte cut (WP19-04 AC12 and WP19-05 AC03); B, a line that is not a record never throws and is reported as malformed_record (AC14 and WP19-05 AC04); C, bad_schema_version for a version that is not an integer (AC17 and WP19-05 AC07); D, a bad complete line, including invalid UTF-8, is skipped and reported as unreadable_record with its line and byte offset, and is not applied lossily (AC13); E, the type checks of the bookkeeping (AC15). The replay function fixes both defects of the store that the red-team reproduced rather than preserving them, and it never writes or repairs anything; the callers make the cut. DEVIATION A changes what the store writes to a log on disk. Before, ProjectStore#_replay takes lastIndexOf('\\n') + 1, a character index, and hands it to fs.truncateSync as a byte offset, so on a log with multi-byte text it cuts into the last good record (18 bytes in the case reproduced) and the next open loses that record; the reader of pull request #365 uses the same index. After, the file is cut at the byte offset of the last 0x0A. DEVIATION B: before, a line of null throws a TypeError out of ProjectStore#_applyRecord and out of Vault#tasksReader, the lines 5, \"s\" and [] are silently accepted, and an entity with no kind or id is stored under the key 'undefined'; after, each is a malformed_record notice and nothing is stored. The input is the bytes of the log, not decoded text, because a decoded string turns invalid bytes into U+FFFD and makes every byte count wrong (114 reported against a true 110 in the case reproduced). A bad complete line in the middle of the log is skipped and reported and every later record is applied; it is not a refusal and never stops the open. Claim E owns the build of PG-19.3 (docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md, the build-layer claim that also holds PG-19.2); the claim row is for the signer to add and is not part of this spec. Depends on contracts: PG-19.2 (Vault#tasksReader and the work port; its pull request #365 must have merged), SO-1.01 (requirement 3: only the vault, the coordinator and the project store name the store; test 'SO-1.01 req 3' in test/project-wiring.test.mjs is not changed), SO-F-02 (the approval conflict rule that stays in project-store.mjs). Boundaries: PG-19.2 owns the facade, src/cli/work-store.mjs and the e2e test, and none of them changes here; a later reader that serves view('task') and conflicts() will also call the shared function and has its own contract, out of scope here; a lock-free read mode that opens the store is out of scope unless a later contract adds one with a proof, on disk beside a live daemon, that it changes nothing; PG-W-21A and PG-W-21B and anything in trust governance (ADR 8) are not touched. Wording of the refusals: the codes future_schema, needs_migration and bad_schema_version are pinned, and so are two phrases of the needs_migration message (the remedy, any daemon command that opens the store migrates it, and that this reader writes nothing), by regular expression, not the whole sentence, which is as of commit 094970a of pull request #365 (red at 58b4e97). Mutants: the table in WP19-04 AC11 maps one to one onto the 15 mutants of the red-team review of pull request #365 (M1 to M15, ids kept), each with its equivalent in the shared module or in the reader's wrapper and the named test that kills it. M1 to M9 are also killed by the golden agreement test (WP19-05 AC10), which compares both callers with literal bytes and literal expected snapshots, so that an agreement between two equally wrong replays cannot pass. Tests are written first and committed alone, every red on an assertion, with the new module imported dynamically inside a try. Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: crdt-merge stays in its own repository and is reached only across the WO-05-A call-out boundary (never vendored, no memev-merge); tiers are free core, Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers, and contact us above that; there is no Federated tier.

tasks.title: One pure shared replay of a project's event log, src/engine/project-replay.mjs: state by kind and id, the store's replacement semantics, the unterminated last line, malformed lines, one refusal policy and fixed notice and refusal ids, with no import
requirements: SR-1.15: no code without a caller. The shared function has two callers in this contract, the store (WP19-05) and the vault's reader (WP19-05); neither is optional (source: docs/scope-one/WBS.md leaf 2.2.15; owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026)

one new module, src/engine/project-replay.mjs, holds the replay of a project's event log as one pure function, so that the project store and the read-only reader cannot drift. It exports exactly these names and no other: REPLAY_NOTICES, REPLAY_REFUSALS, APPROVAL_DECISIONS, unusableApproval, createReplayState, applyRecord, replayLog, schemaVerdict. It has no import at all (the allow-list of static imports is empty), so that it also loads from a copy for a mutation run. It is a module of its own, not part of project-store.mjs, for three reasons: project-store.mjs imports fs, which a pure function cannot; a module that names ProjectStore, projectStore(, coordinator( or new Coordinator would break requirement 3 of SO-1.01 (the regex /ProjectStore|projectStore\(|\bcoordinator\(|new Coordinator/ of test 'SO-1.01 req 3' in test/project-wiring.test.mjs lets only coordinator.mjs, project-store.mjs and vault.mjs match it), so the shared module must not match it; and WP19-01 of PG-19.2 keeps src/cli/work-store.mjs free of ProjectStore, projectStore, project-store and Coordinator, so the reader's port never reaches the store, and a shared module named project-replay.mjs keeps that grep true (source: the replay it extracts from, ProjectStore#_replay and ProjectStore#_applyRecord in src/engine/project-store.mjs, and the second copy of it in Vault#tasksReader in src/engine/vault.mjs, added by pull request #365, PG-19.2, signed)

replayLog(bytes, { truncate = false } = {}) takes the event log as the bytes of the file, a Uint8Array, the JSON Lines in file order, and returns a new state { entities, seq, generation, usedIds, eventKeys, sources, approvals, hlc, notices, cut }: entities is a Map of kind to a Map of id to data; seq and generation are numbers; usedIds is a Set of record ids and entity ids; eventKeys is a Map of idempotency key to the last record that carried it; sources is a Map of 'kind:id' to { id, ts, seq } of the record that last wrote it; approvals is a Map of the id of the log event to { event, id, data }; hlc is the highest well-formed hybrid clock string seen, or null; notices is a list of { code, ... } with code in REPLAY_NOTICES; cut is null or { keep_bytes, dropped_bytes }. An argument that is not a Uint8Array is a caller error and is the one thing the function throws (a TypeError); a fault in the log never throws. The function never re-encodes what it reads: it finds the last 0x0A in the bytes, splits the complete part on 0x0A, decodes each line by itself with a TextDecoder constructed with fatal true, and every byte count it reports is measured on the input bytes. createReplayState() returns the empty state (seq 0, generation 0, hlc null, nothing in any collection, notices [], cut null). applyRecord(state, rec) applies one parsed record to state in place, returns state, and does not change rec; it does not copy either: the state holds rec.entity.data, and rec itself in eventKeys, by reference, and the records that replayLog parses belong to the state it returns and to nothing else, so a caller that needs copies makes them (the reader does, in snapshot). replayLog is createReplayState followed by applyRecord for each line, in line order (source: ProjectStore#_replay and ProjectStore#_applyRecord in project-store.mjs)

replacement keeps the store's semantics: a record is applied in file order, whatever its seq, hlc or gen say; a later write of the same kind and id replaces the data wholesale and never merges, the position of the id in its kind is where it first appeared, and sources names the later record; no record is ever removed: every record id stays in usedIds and every approval event stays in approvals even when two events carry the same approval id ('every approval write is its own event: a later write with the same id replaces the entity, never the event'); a record whose entity data is null leaves the id with a null value (a tombstone is the null, not a deletion); a kind that no store declares is kept as it arrived, and the callers decide what they serve (source: ProjectStore#_applyRecord in project-store.mjs; PG-19.2 reader)

bookkeeping and refusal: for every well-formed record, refused or not, a record id that is a non-empty string is added to usedIds, a well-formed hlc (the pattern of parseHlc in src/engine/oplog.mjs: 13 digits, a dot, 4 or more digits) replaces state.hlc when its (ms, counter) pair, both compared as numbers and not as text, is higher, and seq becomes the larger of seq and the record's seq when that is a finite number. A refused record (refused is truthy) then stops: it adds no entity, no key, no source, no approval and no generation. Any other well-formed record sets generation to the larger of generation and (its gen when a finite number, else 0) plus 1, with or without an entity, and an idempotency key that is a non-empty string is kept in eventKeys. DEVIATION E (its own criterion, WP19-04 AC15; undeclared until this spec): the checks of type above are new. Before, a record id or a key that is a number or another truthy non-string entered usedIds or eventKeys, a seq or gen that is a string was coerced by Math.max and by +, so that a gen of '3' makes the generation the string '31', and a malformed hlc was dropped by parseHlc but the counters were not compared as numbers by any text rule of the module's own; after, a non-string or empty id or key enters nothing, a string or other non-number seq or gen counts as 0, a malformed hlc is ignored, and the counters compare as numbers. The shared function never decides to refuse a write: it only reads what the log holds (source: ProjectStore#_applyRecord in project-store.mjs)

lines: the complete part of the log is split on 0x0A, and the line number of a line is its 1-based place in that split (empty lines counted) and its offset is the byte offset of its first byte in the input. An empty line (no bytes) is skipped without a notice. A line whose bytes are not valid UTF-8, or whose text is not valid JSON, is not applied and not decoded in a lossy way: it gives one notice 'unreadable_record' with its line and offset, and every record after it is applied, as the store does for a line that is not JSON today (DEVIATION D, its own criterion, WP19-04 AC13: today the store reads the file as text, so invalid bytes become U+FFFD and a line that is otherwise JSON is applied with altered text; after, such a line is skipped). A line that parses to something that is not a plain object (null, a number, a string, an array, a boolean), and a record that is a plain object but, not being refused, has an entity that is present and is not a plain object or has a kind or an id that is not a non-empty string, is not applied at all (no bookkeeping, no generation) and gives one notice 'malformed_record' with its line and offset (DEVIATION B, its own criterion, WP19-04 AC14: before, a line of null throws a TypeError out of ProjectStore#_applyRecord, so a project with one such line does not open, in the store and in the reader of pull request #365 alike; the lines 5, "s" and [] are silently accepted; and an entity with no kind or no id is stored under the key 'undefined'). A record that is a plain object with no entity (including {}) is not malformed: it advances the generation and nothing else. A bad complete line in the middle of the log is skipped and reported, never a refusal, and never stops the open (source: ProjectStore#_replay in project-store.mjs; a deviation from the store, stated)

the unterminated last line: when the input does not end in 0x0A, the bytes after the last 0x0A (all of the input when there is none) are the torn tail. They are never applied by any caller, whatever they hold (half a record, a whole valid record, invalid JSON, invalid UTF-8, a cut inside a multi-byte character), and give one notice 'torn_last_line' with dropped_bytes in both modes, because the shared function returns the notices (the reader drops them). Only with truncate true (the store) does the state carry cut { keep_bytes, dropped_bytes }, the number of bytes of the input up to and including the last 0x0A (0 when there is none) and the number after it, so that the store can cut the file at keep_bytes; with truncate false (the reader) cut is null, because the reader never writes and another process may be in the middle of that line; an input that ends in 0x0A has no torn tail and cut is null in both modes. The function never writes, never repairs and never changes the bytes it is given; the callers make the cut. DEVIATION A (its own criterion, WP19-04 AC12 here and WP19-05 AC03 in the callers): cutting the torn last line at a byte offset. This changes what the store writes to a log on disk. Before: ProjectStore#_replay reads the file as text, takes lastIndexOf('\n') + 1, which is a character index, and passes it to fs.truncateSync, which takes a byte offset; with any multi-byte character before the torn line the offset is smaller than the real one, so the file is cut inside the last good record and that record is lost at the next open (measured on a log with accented and CJK text and a torn tail: 843 bytes before open and 791 after, and the log then holds a line that no longer parses; the reader of pull request #365 passes the same text through the same character index). The byte count is also wrong when the file holds invalid UTF-8 (114 reported against a true 110), because the decoded text has replacement characters. After: the store cuts the file at cut.keep_bytes measured on the bytes it read, so every complete line is kept byte for byte and only the torn tail is dropped; for an all-ASCII log nothing differs (source: ProjectStore#_replay in project-store.mjs; a deviation from the store, stated)

approvals: an approval record whose data cannot be used by the conflict rule (a decision outside APPROVAL_DECISIONS, or a resolves that is not a list of event ids, as unusableApproval says) is kept as an entity, stays out of approvals, and gives a notice 'approval_unusable' with the event id and the reason; the reason text is the text the store reports today. unusableApproval and APPROVAL_DECISIONS move here from project-store.mjs, which imports them and keeps exporting APPROVAL_DECISIONS. The derivation of conflicts (analyseApprovals, _derive) stays in project-store.mjs and is not part of this module; the approvals map is what a later reader would pass to it. The notices come in this order: torn_last_line first, then unreadable_record and malformed_record in line order, then approval_unusable in record order, which is the order of the store's recovered list today (source: unusableApproval and ProjectStore#_replay in project-store.mjs)

schemaVerdict(version, { supported, migrate }) is the refusal policy both callers share, and the only place its texts live. version is the schema_version the caller read from meta.json, or supported when there is no meta.json or its schema_version key is absent; a key that is present is passed as it is, null included. It returns { ok: true, migrate: false } when version equals supported; { ok: true, migrate: true } when version is lower and migrate is true (the store); and otherwise { ok: false, code, message } with code in REPLAY_REFUSALS: 'future_schema' when version is higher, 'needs_migration' when version is lower and migrate is not true (the reader), and 'bad_schema_version' when version is not a whole number of 1 or more (DEVIATION C, its own criterion, WP19-04 AC17 and WP19-05 AC07). What is pinned is the code and what the message must say, not the exact sentence: the code 'needs_migration' and a message that names the remedy (matching /any daemon command that opens the store migrates it/) and says the reader writes nothing (matching /this reader writes nothing/); the code 'future_schema' and a message that names the version found and the version supported and says the found one is newer (matching /newer/). The wording of pull request #365 at its commit 094970a (red at 58b4e97) is the starting text: 'schema version <v> is older than <supported>: any daemon command that opens the store migrates it, and this reader writes nothing, so it cannot read it until then'. The criteria use the two regular expressions above, so a later rewording that keeps both statements passes. Migration itself, and the choice to write, stay in the store (source: ProjectStore#open in project-store.mjs; Vault#tasksReader in pull request #365)

the function is pure: it reads and writes no file, no network, no clock and no source of randomness, makes no timer, reads no host global but the language's own built-ins and one named exception, TextDecoder, constructed with fatal true to decode a line of bytes (Buffer and TextEncoder are not used: the function never re-encodes), never changes its inputs, and returns a state that shares nothing with a second call's. It names no ProjectStore, projectStore(, coordinator( or new Coordinator, because requirement 3 of SO-1.01 (test 'SO-1.01 req 3' in test/project-wiring.test.mjs, which is not changed) lets only the vault, the coordinator and the project store name them (source: contracts/scope-one/specs/SO-1.01-canonical-execution-integration.json; test/project-wiring.test.mjs; the review of PG-W-21A, where purity checked only by grep was bypassed)

fixed id sets: every notice code is in the frozen REPLAY_NOTICES (torn_last_line, unreadable_record, malformed_record, approval_unusable) and every refusal code in the frozen REPLAY_REFUSALS (future_schema, needs_migration, bad_schema_version); the module writes no code of its own where it returns one (source: the review of PG-W-21A, fixed rule ids)

out of scope for this task, by design: the store and the reader calling it (WP19-05), any change to the write path (append, _appendLocked, _record, locking), to compact, to migration and to the derivation of conflicts, a lock-free read mode that opens the store, and a reader for view('task') or conflicts(), which will call this function later and has its own contract; nothing here decides ADR 8 or anything in trust governance
tasks.description: Repo: memev. The project store replays its event log (ProjectStore#_replay and #_applyRecord in src/engine/project-store.mjs), and the read-only reader that pull request #365 adds (Vault#tasksReader in src/engine/vault.mjs, PG-19.2) replays it again by its own copy of the rules, held to the store only by tests. This task extracts the rules into one pure module with no import, src/engine/project-replay.mjs, and tests every rule on its own. It writes the module and its tests; the callers are moved onto it in WP19-05. The state it returns is by kind and id, plus what the store keeps beside it (the sequence, the generation, the used ids, the keys, the sources, the approval events and the highest clock), so that the store can use the same function and not a reduced one. The tests live in test/project-replay.test.mjs and import the not-yet-existing module with a dynamic import inside a try, so a missing module is an assertion failure and never a load error. The ordering in the repository is fixed by the owner of the review: pull request #365 lands first, with its copy and its agreement test, and this contract then moves both callers onto the shared function.

criteria.statement: the module exists and exports exactly REPLAY_NOTICES, REPLAY_REFUSALS, APPROVAL_DECISIONS, unusableApproval, createReplayState, applyRecord, replayLog and schemaVerdict: the three functions that replay and check are functions, the three sets are frozen lists with exactly the codes named in the requirements, and the module has no other export; each test first asserts that the import succeeded and that the export it uses is the right type, so the red run fails on those assertions
